declarations.docstring: An auxiliary type associated with a field, a module, and a natural tensor parameter.
For a coordinate module of sufficiently large rank, the auxiliary tensor-power space admits a direct-sum decomposition into tensor products with representation carriers.
A coordinate-module decomposition can be chosen so that evaluation realizes every summand and intertwines the general linear action.
Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the auxiliary tensor-power space of a finite module decomposes as a direct sum of tensor products.
A tensor-power decomposition can be selected with compatible evaluation maps and a compatible action of the distinguished endomorphism algebra.
A tensor-power decomposition can be chosen whose inverse evaluates each pure tensor from an individual direct-sum component.
The two distinguished endomorphism subalgebras are centralizers of one another in characteristic zero.
In characteristic zero, the auxiliary tensor-power space of a finite module has a direct-sum tensor-product decomposition.
Both distinguished endomorphism algebras are semisimple over a characteristic-zero field.
The centralizer of the permutation-action algebra is the auxiliary endomorphism algebra.
An auxiliary subalgebra of endomorphisms of the tensor-power space.
Every element of the auxiliary endomorphism algebra commutes with the permutation-action algebra.
The general linear group of a coordinate module acts through the centralizer of the permutation-action algebra.
A permutation of the index set induces a linear self-equivalence of the auxiliary tensor-power space.
Permuting tensor factors commutes with applying the same linear endomorphism in every factor.
The permutation action on tensor factors extends linearly to an algebra homomorphism from the permutation group algebra.
The range of the permutation group algebra action is the permutation-action subalgebra.
The subalgebra of tensor-power endomorphisms associated with permutations of tensor factors.
The permutation-action subalgebra carries its induced ring structure.
The permutation-action algebra acts faithfully on the auxiliary tensor-power space.
The permutation-action algebra is semisimple when the base field has characteristic zero.
Every permutation-action endomorphism commutes with the auxiliary endomorphism algebra.
Permutations of tensor factors define a monoid homomorphism into tensor-power endomorphisms.
The auxiliary tensor-power space of a finite module is finite over the base field.
